newsitem.title: FRANCE: Argentine-born writer joins French Academy.
newsitem.headline: Argentine-born writer joins French Academy.

text.p: Argentine-born writer and literary critic Hector Bianciotti joined the French Academy on Thursday as one of the 40 life guardians of the French language.
Bianciotti, 66, wearing the 362-year-old Academy's traditional embroidered uniform, took his seat in a solemn ceremony at the dome-shaped building on the banks of the river Seine.
He was elected by his peers a year ago to succeed the late journalist and historian Andre Frossard.

Bianciotti, born in the Argentine town of Calchin Oeste to a family of Italian descent, first wrote in Spanish. After emigrating to France in 1961 and taking French citizenship in 1981, he decided in 1985 to write in French.
Gently mocking his Argentine accent, writer Jacqueline de Romilly, one of the Academy's two female members, hailed him in a traditional welcoming address as a champion of the French language.
"Even coming from elsewhere and from very far away, one can love our language and become a great French writer," she said.
"Your French language, born from contact with literature, has retained its flavour: this is French as we love it."

Bianciotti's novel "The Treaty of Seasons" and short stories "Love is not Loved" both won French literary prizes for best foreign books. His first novel in French, "Without Christ's Mercy", won the Femina award.
